title: Upscale AI Partners With Nvidia While Competing With It
gist: Upscale AI (raised $500M total, $2B valuation, 300+ staff) disclosed its SkyHammer 115.2 Tb/sec Ethernet-based scale-up switch ASIC and SkyFabriX architecture while partnering with Nvidia to use Spectrum-X ASICs for scale-out. Prickett Morgan notes SkyHammer's per-port scale-up bandwidth is about one-sixth of NVSwitch 5, argues predictable latency may matter more than bandwidth for inference, and sees AMD as a natural beneficiary or acquirer.

insights.claim: CPU SMP/NUMA interconnect standards (CCIX, CXL) largely failed because customers rarely mix CPUs from different vendors and each vendor wanted to innovate and differentiate without waiting on a standards body.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Same logic explains why a universal GPU/XPU scale-up standard may struggle against proprietary NVLink.
insights.locator: Every CPU maker always had its own

insights.claim: A standard for GPU/XPU scale-up networking is expected anyway because markets love competition and Nvidia charges a hefty premium for NVSwitch and NVLink ports.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Premium pricing on NVLink is the economic incentive behind UALink/ESUN-type alternatives.
insights.quote: Substitution is a law of economics
insights.locator: So why do we think there will be a standard version

insights.claim: Nvidia may eventually adopt an industry-standard scale-up network with its own protocol overlays, particularly for AI inference, but has no reason to yield ground in training where it holds most of the market.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Inference is where scale-up lock-in is most likely to erode first.

insights.claim: Nvidia's NVLink Fusion lets custom CPUs and hyperscaler XPUs carry NVLink ports into its rackscale systems, but as far as is known it does not allow customers to put NVLink on both their own CPUs and XPUs and buy only NVSwitch plus a protocol licence.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Watch for any loosening of NVLink licensing as a competitive signal.

insights.claim: Upscale AI has raised $500 million in total, its valuation has doubled to $2 billion and headcount has more than doubled to over 300 since its $200 million Series A in January.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Capital is flowing to challengers to Nvidia's networking stack.

insights.claim: SkyHammer has 115.2 Tb/sec aggregate bandwidth, comparable to the best scale-out ASICs from Cisco, Broadcom and Nvidia, and supports up to 576 accelerators in a single networking tier with 'thousands' possible across tiers.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Single-tier radix of 576 matches Nvidia's multi-tier NVSwitch ceiling; competitive on scale, not per-port speed.
insights.locator: What we do know from reading that slide

insights.claim: At 576 devices SkyHammer gives each about 200 Gb/sec, and at 72 XPUs 1.6 Tb/sec per port (200 GB/sec), about one-sixth of NVSwitch 5/NVLink 5's 1.8 TB/sec, with NVLink 6 on Vera-Rubin NVL72 at 3.6 TB/sec.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Large per-port bandwidth gap to NVLink is the main hurdle for Ethernet-based scale-up.
insights.locator: If you do the math on that 576 devices number

insights.claim: Bandwidth may not matter more than latency for AI inference, and predictable latency is always more important than low latency.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: If true, latency-deterministic Ethernet fabrics can compete with NVLink for inference despite lower bandwidth.
insights.quote: predictable latency is always more important than low latency, as Google has taught us
insights.locator: It is not at all clear that bandwidth matters more than latency

insights.claim: Upscale AI says SkyHammer builds predictable jitter and a 100% lossless fabric into the ASIC from a clean sheet, rather than retrofitting scale-up protocols onto an Ethernet pipeline.
insights.speaker: Arvind Srikumar, SVP product and marketing, Upscale AI
insights.so_what: Company claim; specific latency numbers are yet to be published.
insights.quote: we started with a clean sheet of paper rather than taking an Ethernet fabric and retrofitting the protocols
insights.locator: "One of the most important metrics when it comes to tokens is latency"

insights.claim: SkyHammer runs UALink over Ethernet (UALoE) and ESUN, showing it is an Ethernet switch ASIC underneath; the author had hoped for a higher-radix chip running UALink natively.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Scale-up on tweaked Ethernet is about to be tested in the market.
insights.locator: It is interesting to note that SkyHammer is running UALoE

insights.claim: Building a switch with 2x per-port bandwidth from six ASICs costs about 1.5x per port versus a single 2x device at street prices, so Upscale AI will likely build higher aggregate-bandwidth ASICs.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Economics push switch vendors to faster single ASICs.
insights.locator: Upscale AI will no doubt also create devices

insights.claim: Upscale AI will buy Nvidia Spectrum-X ASICs to build its own scale-out switches (400G, 800G and 1.6T ports) running its SkyOS, a SONiC-based network OS, rather than Quantum-X InfiniBand, as its founders believe Ethernet will conquer InfiniBand.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nvidia monetises Ethernet scale-out even through a scale-up competitor.

insights.claim: SkyOS and the SkyCMD tool span scale-up and scale-out networks, and customers can mix any CPU, GPU or XPU behind a DPU or NIC.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Vendor-neutral fabric is the pitch to non-Nvidia accelerator buyers.
insights.locator: The important thing, according to Upscale AI

insights.claim: Nvidia does not support SkyHammer as an alternative to NVSwitch, so there is currently no way to do scale up with Nvidia GPUs through Upscale AI.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan

insights.claim: AMD is counting on firms like Upscale AI for UALink, UALoE or ESUN scale-up options and may lose patience and acquire Upscale AI.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Possible M&A angle; monitor AMD's scale-up networking strategy.
insights.quote: it may lose patience and just acquire Upscale AI
insights.locator: There is no way - as yet

insights.claim: Nvidia could flatten its NVSwitch network by cutting per-port bandwidth to raise radix, or port NVLink to SkyHammer and become the dominant supplier of UALoE or ESUN switches.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nvidia has options to neutralise Ethernet-based scale-up challengers.

insights.claim: InfiniBand will still beat Ethernet on port-to-port hop latency and Nvidia will keep selling it for HPC and AI, but Ultra Ethernet-compatible switches get closer and scale out further for a given topology.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Ethernet continues to gain share in AI back-end networking.
insights.locator: Some would say with the first generation
